info.bio: Una de las buena bandas norteamericanes de mediados a fines de los 60's y posiblemente una de las más olvidadas y subestimadas de esa época. Spirit no puede ser clasificada en un solo género ya que en su sonido hay elementos de jazz, psicodelia, hard rock y hasta rock progresivo, si nos ponemos más estrictos. El grupo estuvo originalmente compuesto por Randy California (guitarra, voz), Mark Andes (bajo), Jay Ferguson (voz, percusion), Ed Cassidy (batería) y John Locke (teclados y percusión).

scenes.desc: La psicodelia angelina desciende de los Byrds y se divide en varios campos: la novedad pop (Strawberry Alarm Clock), el rave-up crudo de los Seeds, la larga improvisación de Iron Butterfly (que ya titulaban un disco «Heavy» antes del heavy metal), el barroco de Love (Forever Changes) y, sobre todo, los Doors, quizá la banda más creativa de la historia del rock: su primer disco solo contiene obras maestras y Jim Morrison define al cantante de rock como artista. Spirit, Chocolate Watchband y la misa rock de los Electric Prunes completan la escena.

xref.title: Formation Inspiration (Spring 1976)
xref.body: Bernie and Peter were motivated to form a band after witnessing a Sex Pistols gig in Manchester. Despite perceiving the performance as "terrible," they found it "great" in its spirit and decided that if the Sex Pistols could perform, they could too. Their initial group was called Warsaw, which subsequently evolved into Joy Division, and later New Order. "If they could do it, maybe we could."

xref.title: "Smells Like Teen Spirit" Inspiration (1991)
xref.body: One night in 1991, after going out drinking with Kurt Cobain, Kathleen Hannah commented that he smelled "sweet, almost like a particular type of deodorant marketed to teens." Cobain, who never wore deodorant, was inspired by her remark to use "Smells Like Teen Spirit" as the title for a new song. "When they returned to Kurt's place, she remarked that Kurt smelled sweet, almost like a particular type of deodorant marketed to teens."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Aversion to Success and Depression (1991-1992)
xref.body: As "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" grew in popularity, John Frusciante became increasingly unhappy with the band's massive commercial success. He yearned for the underground scene, preferring small clubs over arenas, and his personality shifted from "manic, happy-go-lucky fun" to a more serious and depressed state. This created tension with the band, particularly Anthony Kiedis. He found a kindred spirit in Kurt Cobain of Nirvana, who shared his desire for underground credibility, which further fueled his discontent with the Chili Peppers' mainstream success. "He wanted to be in a cool underground band. The success was way too serious for him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inspiration from The Mansion – Blood Sugar Sex Magik Recording (1991)
xref.body: During the recording of "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" in a historic mansion, John Frusciante embraced the isolated and reputedly haunted environment. Unlike Chad Smith, who refused to stay there, Frusciante loved the house and found it inspirational, ready to disconnect from the outside world. He believed friendly ghosts resided there and even mused that the spirit of a person who died in the house might have influenced his guitar sound. "There are definitely ghosts in this house, said John, but they are very friendly."

xref.title: Shocked by Depeche Mode's Excess (1993)
xref.body: Primal Scream served as an opening act for Depeche Mode's Devotional Tour at Dave Gahan's insistence, as he believed they shared a similar partying spirit. However, the band was reportedly so shocked by the extreme drug use they witnessed that their singer, Bobby Gillespie, was quoted saying Dave Gahan did more drugs than all of Primal Scream combined, leading them to give up drugs entirely. "The story goes that primal scream was so shocked by what they saw that they gave up drugs entirely."

xref.title: Last Concert (March 1, 1994) – Terminal 1, Munich
xref.body: Nirvana's final performance took place on March 1, 1994, in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany, before an audience of approximately 3,000 people. Kurt Cobain was unwell, suffering from a sore throat, and the performance was not up to par, leading to the cancellation of the remainder of the tour so he could recover from chronic bronchitis and laryngitis. "Nirvana's last ever show was staged in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany on March 1, 1994, in front of about 3,000 people."

xref.title: Goat Punishment Secret Shows (November 1998)
xref.body: In November 1998, Weezer played a secret show in Hollywood under the name Goat Punishment, during which they performed six Nirvana songs, including "Swapmate" from *Bleach* and "Aneurysm," the B-side of "Smells Like Teen Spirit." A second Goat Punishment show days later featured Oasis covers. "In November 1998, Weezer played a secret show in Hollywood under the name Goat Punishment, during which they played Swapmate, which is deep on Nirvana's Bleach Amble, and Aneurysm, which you'll find is the B-side of Snows like Teen Spirit."

xref.title: Lakota Spirit Name and Eagle Feather (2016)
xref.body: At an Assembly of First Nations gathering in Gatineau in early December 2016, Gord Downie was presented with an eagle feather and given the Lakota spirit name "Omani," meaning "the man who walks among the stars." "He did appear at a gathering of the Assembly of First Nations and Gattanoqua back at early December 2016, where he was presented with an eagle feather, and given a Lakota spirit name, a copy of Omani, the man who walks among the stars."

xref.body: Due to the relentless deterioration caused by Alzheimer's, Spirit of the West concluded their career with a farewell performance in 2016. xref.title: Accused of Plagiarism for "Stairway to Heaven"
xref.body: Jimmy Page, guitarist for Led Zeppelin, was accused by Randy California of Spirit (and his estate) of ripping off the guitar arpeggio from Spirit's instrumental "Taurus" for Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven." This led to a contentious, years-long court battle that concluded at the Supreme Court in 2020, with the court ultimately rejecting the plagiarism claim. "For years, Randy California, lead guy at Spirits, and then his estate after he died, claimed that Jimmy Page ripped off Taras for Stairway to Heaven."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Alleged Inspiration for The Passenger
xref.body: The Doors singer Jim Morrison is allegedly the inspiration behind Iggy Pop's song "The Passenger." Legend suggests Iggy once owned Morrison's old leather pants and believed Jim's spirit had passed to him through them. "The song was allegedly inspired by Dora Singer Jim Morrison. In fact, legend has it that Iggy once owned a pair of Jim's old leather pants, and that Iggy believed Morrison's spirit had passed to him from those pants."

xref.title: Band Name Origin and Mis-translation
xref.body: The name "Depeche Mode" was adopted from a French fashion magazine. For many years, it was commonly, but incorrectly, translated as "fast fashion." The more accurate translation, reflecting the spirit of the original French, should be "fashion news update." "Your name depech mode was taken from the title of a French fashion magazine. I heard that. And for years, that has been wrongly translated as fast fashion."

xref.body: Utilizing some of his earnings, Brian "Dexter" Holland became a certified jet pilot and owns a private jet. "Oh, and did I mention that Dexter used some of his earnings to become a certified jet pilot?"

xref.title: Claimant in "Stairway to Heaven" Lawsuit
xref.body: Randy California, the lead guitarist for Spirit, and later his estate after his death, claimed for years that Jimmy Page plagiarized Spirit's instrumental "Taurus" for the iconic guitar arpeggio in Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven." He sought a share of the estimated $500 million net worth of "Stairway to Heaven" through a contentious lawsuit that went all the way to the Supreme Court in 2020 before being ultimately dismissed. "For years, Randy California, lead guy at Spirits, and then his estate after he died, claimed that Jimmy Page ripped off Taras for Stairway to Heaven."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Collaboration with Ministry
xref.body: Several members of Front 242 contributed directly to Ministry's "groundbreaking records" during the mid-80s, assisting in Ministry's stylistic transition and highlighting a collaborative spirit within the emerging industrial scene. "Several members of Front II-IV II actually helped in Ministries' transition by appearing on those groundbreaking records of the mid-80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Considered "Too Light" for Punk
xref.body: In the mid-2000s, Hedley was categorized as a band that was "too light" or "too poppy for punk." This led to alt-rock radio stations refusing to play their music, citing that their fans were "too young" and lacked the "true spirit of punk and alternative music." Audiences would immediately complain upon hearing their songs. "groups like Headley and Simple Plan and Good Charlotte were maybe a little too light."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Considered "Too Pop for Alternative"
xref.body: Despite her pop punk association, Avril Lavigne was often perceived as "too pop to be alternative," leading to resistance from some alt-rock radio stations and audiences. Her fans were sometimes criticized for being "too young" and not embodying the "true spirit of punk and alternative music." "but was considered to be too pop to be alternative."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Contemporary Goth-ish Sound
xref.body: Interpol, hailing from New York, is considered one of the best-known contemporary bands that, while "Goth or at least Goth-ish," seeks to preserve the spirit of 1979 Goth. "Interpol, one of the best known of the contemporary Goth or at least Goth-ish bands that seek to keep alive the spirit of 1979."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Continued Performance and Stem Cell Treatment
xref.body: John Mann continued performing with Spirit of the West for as long as his deteriorating condition allowed. In 2015, he sought experimental stem cell treatment in Mexico in an attempt to combat the progression of Alzheimer's. "John kept performing as long as he could. There was some stem cell treatment in Mexico in 2015."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Critical Decline in the 80s
xref.body: During the mid-to-late 1980s, Bowie's music and performances, including albums like "Tonight" and "Never Let Me Down," and the "Glass Spiders tour," faced harsh criticism, with descriptions like "tired" and "fake enthusiasm" being used to characterize his work, suggesting a departure from his earlier innovative spirit. "Words like tired and phrases like fake enthusiasm were thrown around."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cult Following and Influences
xref.body: Despite being dismissed by many for their unconventional style, the New York Dolls developed a significant following among those who appreciated "weird things." They were seen by some as embodying the true spirit of rock and roll, where attitude and energy surpassed virtuosity. The band regularly played alongside other influential artists like Iggy Pop and KISS. "Soon, the dolls were playing regular gigs alongside Iggy Pop, and a band who took the makeup thing even further."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cult Pop Punk/Garage Rock Artist
xref.body: Ty Segall was cited as an example of a "culty band" (artist) that plumbed Pop Punk styles in the 2010s, sometimes taking things harder and mixing in elements of garage rock. These artists kept the spirit of Pop Punk alive during a decade when it experienced a brief surge, though not reaching the popularity of its 90s and 2000s waves. "Some examples included waves, bass drum of death, Thai seagull and Toronto's pop."

xref.title: Cultural Icon of Political Punk
xref.body: The Clash, particularly through Joe Strummer, were regarded as the quintessential political and activist punk band, embodying a defiant spirit that resonated with millions worldwide and refused to compromise. "He was the political punk, the activist punk, the punk that refused to bend. For millions around the world, he was the guy who embodied the best of the punk spirit."

xref.title: D.D. Ramone's Role
xref.body: D.D. Ramone became the main songwriter and lyricist for the Ramones for 15 years, despite his playing style consisting of long runs of the same notes. His spirit and raw energy were more impactful than technical prowess. "D.D. became the main songwriter and the lyricist for the Ramones for 15 years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dee Dee Ramone – Self-Taught "Primitive" Bassist and Primary Lyricist
xref.body: Dee Dee Ramone came to the bass without prior knowledge of how to play it, embodying the punk ethos of "anyone can do it." Despite his basic technique, he became the Ramones' primary lyricist and a massive influence on a generation of musicians. His primitive approach was not a limitation but a defining feature. "A 'primitive' bassist who, without initially knowing how to play, embodied the punk spirit of 'anyone can do it' and was the band's main lyricist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: Peter Hook was interviewed earlier in the year for a film documentary on "the spirit of radio CFNY years" (1977 to 1992), with the interview taking place in London. "I was at Peter Hook's house earlier this year. We are doing a documentary, a film documentary on the spirit of radio CF and Y years."

xref.title: Early Onset Alzheimer's Diagnosis
xref.body: John Mann, the singer for Spirit of the West, was diagnosed with early onset Alzheimer's in 2014, when he was in his early 50s. This uncommon form of the disease affects individuals before age 65, accounting for less than 10% of all cases. His diagnosis came while he was in remission from colorectal cancer, which had been diagnosed in 2009. "John was diagnosed with early onset Alzheimer's."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: After the release of their debut album in 2001, Staggered Crossing embarked on tours with notable acts such as Nickelback, The Guess Who, Midnight Oil, Spirit of the West, Blue Rodeo, and Big Sugar, among others. "From there they toured with Nickelback, the Guess Who, Midnight Oil, Spirited the West, Blurodio, Big Sugar and others."

xref.body: The Clash are described as having a Garage Rock core because of their "back to basics approach," aligning them with the fundamental spirit of the genre despite their punk rock context. "The sex pistols, the clash, the damned, all those groups are garage rock bands at their core because of their back to basics approach."

xref.title: Inspiration for "Smells Like Teen Spirit"
xref.body: Tobi Vail once dated Kurt Cobain. In 1991, during a visit to his apartment, she spray-painted "Kurt smells like teen spirit" on his wall, remarking that he smelled "fruity and perfumed" like a brand of deodorant she knew. Kurt, unaware of the deodorant brand, interpreted it as a comment on his youthful vitality and used it as a title for a song. "She then spray painted Kurt smells like teen spirit on his wall. Now, Kurt, who did not wear deodorant, thought she was commenting on his youthful vitality and thought, hmm, that would make a good title for a song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

xref.title: Inspirational and Unconventional Artist
xref.body: Patti Smith inspired both men and women with her distinctive "I don't give a crap view of the world, the universe, and beyond," and her uncompromising approach to her art. Her vocal delivery was described as unlike anything heard before, embodying a spirit of doing things her own way. "Patty was an inspiration to so many women and men with her techno prisoners I don't give a crap view of the world, the universe, and beyond."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inspired by "Kurt Smells Like Teen Spirit"
xref.body: In 1991, Kathleen Hanna spray-painted "Kurt smells like teen spirit" on his apartment wall, intending it as a joke about a fruit-infused deodorant. Kurt, misunderstanding it as a comment on his rebellious spirit, liked the phrase and used it as a song title for Nirvana, creating one of their most famous tracks. "she spray-painted Kurt smells like teen spirit on the wall of his apartment, teen spirit being this fruit-infused deodorant for girls. Kurt, who apparently didn't bother with deodorant, thought that Kathleen was commenting on his youthful sense of rebellion. He liked what she wrote. He then wrote a song with that title, which worked out okay."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Inspired by Kathleen Hannah
xref.body: Kurt Cobain was "accidentally inspired" to write the song "Smells Like Teen Spirit" by Kathleen Hannah. "And the woman who accidentally inspired Kurt Cobain to write a song called Smells Like Teen Spirit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kindred Spirit with Kate Bush
xref.body: Tori Amos was immediately compared to Kate Bush upon her solo debut, with listeners recognizing them as kindred spirits due to their fearless and unique approaches to self-expression, despite not being identical in style. "anyone familiar with Kate Bush's headspace, which is somewhere beyond the orbit of Saturn, immediately recognized that she and Tori were kindred spirits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kurt Cobain's "Teen Spirit" Inspiration
xref.body: In 1991, after a night of drinking, Kathleen Hanna (of Bikini Kill) spray-painted "Kurt smells like teen spirit" on Kurt Cobain's apartment wall, mocking him because she thought he smelled like a fruit-infused girls' deodorant called Teen Spirit. Kurt, unaware of the deodorant, interpreted the phrase as a comment on his rebellious youthful spirit, which inspired him to write a song with that title. "In 1991, she made fun of Kurt after a night of drinking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kurt Cobain's Plagiarism Concerns
xref.body: While writing "Nevermind," Kurt Cobain was frequently troubled by the thought that he might be inadvertently plagiarizing other artists. He worried about similarities between "Smells Like Teen Spirit" and Boston's "More Than a Feeling," as well as the quiet/loud structure resembling The Pixies' style. He also considered how Jazz Coleman might react to "Come As You Are." "Yet as he was writing it, Kurt Cobain was nagged by the thought that he just might be ripping off other people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mode of Move Cooperative Label – Communist/Collective Label Run by Bands Including Future Manager Alan White
xref.body: Mode of Move stood for Modern Dance Music. Co-founder Alan White is still the band's manager today. The label operated as a collective, with bands meeting at a house on Columbia Street to divide up responsibilities: mailing cassettes to college stations, writing letters, organizing hall shows. The anarcho-cooperative spirit of the whole enterprise was very much in line with the Vancouver underground scene of the time. "We had these meetings as if we were revolutionaries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musician Friends' Benefit Concerts
xref.body: John Mann's musician friends, including members of the Barenaked Ladies, Blue Rodeo, and Sarah McLachlan, regularly organized benefit concerts to help fund his medical treatments. These events often featured collective performances of Spirit of the West classics. "And whenever one of these benefits was held, everybody joins in on this Spirit of the West class."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Past Relationship with Kurt Cobain
xref.body: Kathleen Hanna once dated Kurt Cobain. During this time, she famously spray-painted "Kurt smells like teen spirit" on his apartment wall in 1991, which inadvertently became the title of a Nirvana song. "and she once dated Kurt Cobain, which brings me to this story."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pixies Influence
xref.body: Kurt Cobain specifically sought to write "Smells Like Teen Spirit" in the style of the Pixies, known for their distinct loud/soft/loud/soft dynamic shifts in their music. He later candidly described this creative process as an attempt to "rip off the Pixies." "He later called the whole exercise an attempt to rip off the Pixies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pop Punk Heritage Act
xref.body: Blink-182 was identified as one of the "Big Heritage Acts" of Pop Punk that kept the spirit of the genre alive in the 2010s, despite its popularity being nowhere near its 90s or 2000s peaks. There was also a sentiment in some punk circles to reclaim punk from "Corporatized Punk" exemplified by bands like Blink-182. "The Big Heritage Acts were still there, you know, offspring, link quantity to some 41 simple plan, and they kept the spirit alive." "There's also the sense in some quarters that Punk needs to be torn down and rebuilt, reclaimed from the so-called Croppered Punk, exemplified by Blink-Wentety 2-Some41 in the offspring."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Quintessential American New Wave Band
xref.body: The B-52s are described as the quintessential American New Wave band, embodying the genre's spirit through their unique blend of catchy music, playful approach, and fashionably silly aesthetic. "B-52s were the only American quintessential new wave band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Resilience in Attawapiskat
xref.body: Despite Attawapiskat being in the news for serious issues like housing crises, a major suicide epidemic, and drug problems, Adrian Sutherland and others like him refuse to give up on their home and neighbors, highlighting a spirit of resilience. "From Anna Wapisgad in Northern Ontario, a place that's been in the news for so many sad reasons like housing crisis, a major suicide epidemic, drug problems and more. But guys like Adrian Sutherland refused to give up on their home and their neighbors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Riot Grrrl Pioneers
xref.body: Bikini Kill, led by Kathleen Hanna and Tobi Vail, epitomized the Riot Grrrl movement. They were deeply involved in feminist politics, advocating for safe spaces for women at shows by urging them to the front while "dudes" went to the back. They also published zines, aligning with the DIY spirit of the movement. "They were heavily into feminist politics. They favored women at their shows, urging them down fronts and dudes to the back. Meaning that gigs be safe places for women? Check. Publishing zines? Yep, that too. And was the music loud and angry? You bet."

xref.title: Strategic Single Release and Unforeseen Success
xref.body: On August 27, 1991, an advanced single (likely "Smells Like Teen Spirit") was sent to alternative radio stations, not as the band's or label's first choice, but as a marketing tactic to "break the ice with the freaks." Expectations for the album were so low that selling 100,000 copies would have been thrilling, with only 46,251 copies initially manufactured for stores. However, the song's radio debut caused an explosion of listener demand, leading to immediate sell-outs and rapid weekly sales of 300,000 copies within two months, demonstrating the sudden mobilization of Generation X. "expectations were really low. If this album eventually sold 100,000 copies, everybody, including the band, would be thrilled."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide and Legacy
xref.body: Jim Ellison, the singer for Material Issue, tragically committed suicide, which derailed the band's career. His life and music left a lasting impact, inspiring The Tragically Hip's song "Escape is at Hand for the Traveling Man" and being honored by the annual "International Pop Over Throw" festival in Chicago. "However, their spirit lives on. Chicago, host an annual festival called International Pop Over Throw that's been going on since 1997, and it features bands in the whole PowerPop vein."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Teen Spirit Deodorant Connection
xref.body: Kathleen Hannah, a member of the all-girl punk band Bikini Kill, was the person who coined the phrase "Kurt smells like teen spirit," referring to the fruity-smelling deodorant brand. This deodorant was also the "deodorant of choice of Toby Vale," another member of Bikini Kill and Kurt Cobain's girlfriend. "Now, you may or may not know this, but teen spirit is a fruity smelling brand of deodorant that girls wear."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The World's Greatest Drinking Song
xref.body: One of Spirit of the West's most popular songs within the Celtic diaspora was written during a 1989 tour of England. It originated as a humorous piece about the band's misbehavior in pubs on that tour and was never intended to be recorded. However, an album producer heard it and insisted the group complete it, despite it never being officially released as a single. It has since become one of Canada's, and the world's, greatest drinking songs. "It was never supposed to be recorded, but their producer for one of their albums heard it and demanded that the group finish it. Nevertheless, it was never, ever officially released as a single. Yet somehow, this has become one of Canada's. One of the worlds greatest drinking songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tragic End of Singer
xref.body: Material Issue's career was "derailed by the sudden suicide of singer Jim Ellison." Despite this tragedy, their spirit continues, notably through an annual Powerpop festival in Chicago named "International Pop Over Throw," inspired by their album title. "I love these guys, but they were derailed by the sudden suicide of singer Jim Ellison."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Trailblazer and Rhythm Player
xref.body: Joan Jett is recognized as a trailblazer in rock music, primarily for her hard-riffing rhythm guitar style rather than virtuoso soloing. Her pioneering spirit, especially as a member of The Runaways, places her as a significant figure. "Joan belongs on this list because she was a trailblazer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Barker's Footwear and Headwear Lines for DC Shoes
xref.body: In addition to his own clothing company, Famous Stars and Straps, Travis Barker also designed a line of skate shoes and hats for DC Shoes. This demonstrates his entrepreneurial spirit beyond his role as a drummer. "And if that wasn't enough, Travis created a skate shoe and a line of hats for a company called DC Shoes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unconventional Stage Appearance
xref.body: In contrast to the typical punk aesthetic, all three members of Husker Dü appeared on stage in street clothes, eschewing common punk fashion like leather jackets or mohawk haircuts. This choice underscored their independent spirit and focus on musical substance over image. "All three members appeared on stage in street clothes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Wife of Adam Horowitz
xref.body: Kathleen Hannah is married to Adam Horowitz, and she is known for being a member of the Riot Girl band Bikini Kill. "He's currently married to Kathleen Hannah. She of the Riot Girl Band Bikini Kill and the woman who accidentally inspired Kurt Cobain to write a song called Smells Like Teen Spirit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: X-Large Skate Clothing Company
xref.body: The Beastie Boys have ventured into the fashion industry by owning a skate clothing company called X-Large, demonstrating their entrepreneurial spirit beyond music. "The Beastie Boys have a skate clothing company called X-Large."
